title: I built a browser mech arena and learned that game feel needs a deliberate pass
author: Due-Entertainment953
selftext:
I built Mech Arena, a small top-down browser combat prototype. The player moves, aims, shoots enemies, collects scrap, chooses a module after each wave, and tries to survive a boss.

Play it here:
https://b087dde9-71f4-4e48-a9e6-a01e78130132.aippy.live

I used Freebuff as part of the AI-assisted coding workflow. It helped me turn the written design into a playable prototype, but I still had to test the result and decide what was actually fun. The first build had the systems but felt flat because hits and rewards were not obvious.

I revised the feedback layer so damage numbers, +scrap, critical-hit messages, wave-clear callouts, impact particles, and heat feedback appear immediately during play. That was a useful lesson: adding more features is not the same as making the core action readable and satisfying.

I would appreciate feedback on the controls, enemy readability, and whether the screen communicates too much at once. This is a free prototype, not a commercial service.
